title: Three P's
concept: After this one you can give a green light only with a safety net and a backbone behind it.
bookIdea: Steiner describes a permission as a yes, with a reason the person can accept, that frees them from an old order, and says it works only if the giver also provides protection for the fear that follows and has the potency, the strength, to stand behind it.

opener.setting: Wednesday, 6:50pm, Halden, the third floor, by the station. The office is nearly empty, and Clara has been at her desk since five.

lines.text: “I've been here since five. Nobody's told me yet, and the demo's on Thursday.”
lines.cue: hands flat on the desk, not quite looking up

opener.ask: Which parts of a yes make it safe to give?

rounds.label: Spot, round 1
rounds.intro: A yes that holds has three parts, and all three are yours to bring. The green light is the yes itself, with a reason the other person can accept. The safety net is you being there when the fear arrives. The backbone is your strength to keep the yes standing when someone pushes against it.

items.text: “Yes, run the Thursday demo on your own. You rebuilt the pricing sheet in a day when Omar was out, so you can do this.”
items.cue: to Clara, pen in your hand, smiling
items.why: That is the yes, and it comes with a reason Clara can check against her own week. A green light with a reason she believes is one she can use.

traps.1: The safety net. Nothing in the line says what happens if the demo goes wrong. It gives a yes and a reason.
traps.2: The backbone. Nobody is pushing against the yes in this line, so there is nothing to hold yet.

items.example:
Driving school, Saturday, 9:00am.
Learner: “Can I take the car up the hill on my own?”
Instructor: “Yes. You held the clutch perfectly on Tuesday, so you're ready.”

items.text: “If it goes wrong, call me. I'll be on the line, and plan B is on the shared drive.”
items.cue: to Clara, one hand on the back of her chair
items.why: That is the net. It says who catches the fall and how fast, so the fear that comes after the yes has somewhere to go.

traps.0: The green light. The yes is already given. This line is about what happens when it wobbles.
traps.2: The backbone. Promising to be there is the net. The backbone is about holding the yes when somebody pushes against it.

items.example:
Trek to the lake, 6:00am, the base camp.
Guide: “If the weather turns, we come down the east path, and I'll radio the hut.”
Walker: “Good. That's the plan.”

items.text: “Daniel says Clara is too new for the client. I've told him the yes stands, and I'll say it again in the meeting.”
items.cue: to Clara, in the corridor, voice level
items.why: That is the backbone. Someone is pushing against the yes, and you keep it standing. A yes that folds when the first person objects was never a yes she could lean on.

traps.0: The green light. The yes was given earlier. This line is about keeping it standing.
traps.1: The safety net. A net catches a fall. This line is about stopping the yes from being pulled away in the first place.

items.example:
Swimming pool, Saturday, 8:00am.
Parent: “She's too young for the deep end.”
Coach: “I've said she can go in, and she will. I'll be on the steps.”
The girl climbs down the ladder.

rounds.label: Play, the week in motion
rounds.intro: Two scenes. Watch what each yes does to the other person, what happens when the net is missing, and what a yes does when someone leans on it.

items.title: Wednesday, 6:50pm, the third floor
items.setting: Halden, by the station. The lights are off over the empty rows, and the demo file is open on Clara's screen.

beats.text: “Can I run the Thursday demo on my own? Just tell me yes or no.”
beats.cue: hands flat on the desk, not quite looking at you

lines.outcome: The scene stops there. Clara says thanks in a flat voice and turns back to her slides, with nothing to hold if the client pushes.
lines.why: A bare green light is a yes with the net cut away. It feels generous for a second, and then the person is alone with the risk you handed over.

lines.text: “Yes. You rebuilt the pricing sheet in a day when Omar was out, so you can do this. And if it breaks, I'm on the call with a plan B on the shared drive.”
lines.outcome: Clara exhales and starts reading the plan B slides. She says it is the first time all week she has stopped bracing.
lines.why: You give the yes, a reason from her own week that she can accept, and the safety net in one breath. She knows she will not be left alone if it wobbles.

lines.outcome: Clara's shoulders drop. “Thursday's too late to prep,” she says, and goes back to her slides.
lines.why: A delay is not a green light. It is a shrug, and it leaves her guessing for the rest of the evening.

beats.text: “And if the client asks something I don't know?”

lines.text: “Then you'll have to think on your feet.”
lines.outcome: She looks at the screen and doesn't say anything for a while.
lines.why: This hands the risk back to her with no way to carry it. It sounds like a shrug, and it leaves her with the fear.

lines.text: “Say you'll come back by Friday with the answer. I'll be on the call, and I'll back you up.”
lines.outcome: Clara writes “Friday, with the pricing notes” on the pad and underlines it twice.
lines.why: That is the net again, now in a sentence she can say in the room. It also says you will stand next to her, which keeps the yes from feeling like a dare.

lines.text: “Just say you don't know. Everyone does.”
lines.outcome: She nods, but she writes the question on the pad anyway.
lines.why: This is kind, but it is a shrug with a smile. It isn't a plan, so she has nothing to hold if the client pushes.

beats.text: “I'm not sure I can carry all of it. Pricing is the bit I always get wrong.”
beats.cue: looking at the lights on the road by the station

lines.text: “You'll be fine. Don't worry about it.”
lines.outcome: She nods and goes back to the slides, but she doesn't look convinced.
lines.why: Reassurance with no reason behind it. It sounds warm, and it gives her nothing to stand on.

lines.text: “I said yes and I'm keeping it. Run the pricing slide for me now, and we'll fix whatever wobbles tonight.”
lines.outcome: Clara laughs, a bit surprised, and runs the slide twice. The second time she doesn't stop at the figures.
lines.why: This is the backbone. You keep the yes in place when she wobbles, and you push a little where the wobble is, so the old doubt has to deal with your strength as well as hers.

lines.text: “Then don't do it. Let Daniel handle the pricing.”
lines.outcome: The scene stops there. Clara sits back, a bit smaller, and says she'll stick to the easy slides.
lines.why: This takes the yes back at the first wobble and calls it kindness. A green light that folds when the job gets hard has no backbone, and that is the trap.

items.payoff: Thursday, 11:20am. Clara runs the demo with no plan B. When the client asks about pricing she has nothing to point at, and Daniel answers for her in the room. She doesn't speak again until the end.

fallout.them: Clara closes the laptop and walks past the lift without saying goodnight.

items.example:
Printing shop, by the station, 7:30pm.
Owner: “Can I leave the shop with you for an hour? Just say yes.”
You: “Yes, and if anything goes wrong I'm two lanes away.”

items.title: Friday, 4:40pm, the server corner
items.setting: Halden, third floor. Omar is leaning on the server rack with one hand pressed to his lower back. The payment fix is ready, and the release window closes at eleven.

beats.text: “I want to ship the payment fix tonight without the second review. I've seen this bug before. Just say yes.”
beats.cue: not sitting down, not quite standing straight

lines.outcome: The scene stops there. Omar nods and turns back to his laptop. The build goes into the queue, and nobody has checked the refund path.
lines.why: A bare yes with no net. If the fix breaks, Omar carries it alone, and you carry the knowledge that you signed off a check nobody ran.

lines.text: “Yes. Ship it once the refund test passes, and I'll sit with you on the diff at seven.”
lines.outcome: Omar looks surprised, then relieved. “Seven, then,” he says, and starts the refund test.
lines.why: The yes comes with a net: the refund test first, and a check at seven that you will be there for. He is not left to carry the risk by himself.

lines.outcome: Omar sighs. “Monday's the release. Fine,” he says, and goes back to his screen.
lines.why: A delay with no reason. It takes the yes away and leaves him to decide alone, which is much the same as having no net.

beats.text: “It's always the same, isn't it? Nobody trusts me with the release.”
beats.cue: a short laugh that isn't really a laugh

lines.text: “You're right, nobody does. Why don't you go home?”
lines.outcome: The scene stops there. Omar's face closes, and he stops talking about the fix altogether.
lines.why: This agrees with the sting and then pushes him out. It looks like sympathy, but it hands him the verdict and takes you out of the job.

lines.text: “I do trust you, Omar. That's why I want the refund test to run first.”
lines.outcome: Omar stops rubbing his back for a second. “Okay,” he says. “Fair enough.”
lines.why: This gives him a reason to be believed, and a check that protects him too. The trust shows in the test, not only in the words.

lines.outcome: Omar shrugs and shuts the laptop. “Forget it.”
lines.why: The request is right, but the tone is sharp. Omar hears a verdict on himself, and the test now feels like a punishment.

beats.text: “Seven o'clock, then. Don't bail on me.”
beats.cue: pointing at you with the pen

lines.text: “I won't. Bring the old bug notes, and I'll bring the diff.”
lines.outcome: He nods, and the corridor lights click off as he heads for the coffee machine.
lines.why: The net only works if you turn up. You name what each of you will bring, so both people leave with a job, not a promise.

lines.text: “Fine, but if it breaks, it's on you.”
lines.outcome: The scene stops there. Omar's jaw sets. “Right. Forget seven.” He pushes the release through alone.
lines.why: This is a green light with the net cut and a sting attached. He will remember the sting, not the review.

lines.outcome: He says thanks, but he doesn't look at you again before he goes.
lines.why: It sounds easy, and it lets him ship without a plan. A yes with nothing behind it is only half a yes.

items.payoff: Friday, 11:50pm. The payment fix goes out without the review. For two hours the refund path fails, and Omar answers the calls alone. The yes you gave is the first thing the team mentions on Monday.

fallout.them: Omar goes home without saying goodbye, and the seven o'clock check never happens.

rounds.label: Analyse, explain it
rounds.intro: Two explanations to check. Name the part that was missing, and when a big yes should wait.

items.text: “Yes. Go on, it's yours.” That was the whole of it, and then the demo went wrong.
items.cue: in the corridor, the week after. Which explanation fits?
options: Protection was missing. The green light came with no safety net, so Clara was alone with the fear when the demo wobbled. Steiner says the fear arrives after the step is taken, and the giver has to be there for it.
Permission was too strong. A green light should always come with a warning, not a yes.
Potency was the only thing missing. Clara lacked the skill, so no yes would have helped her.
items.why: A permission works when protection stands behind it. Steiner says a person who drops an old order often feels alone and scared afterwards, and without a giver ready to catch them they slide back. This yes had the first part only.

traps.1: Permission too strong. It sounds careful, but a warning gives Clara nothing to hold. The yes then sounds like a risk you are handing her to carry.
traps.2: Potency missing, and it is Clara's skill. Steiner puts potency in the giver: it is the strength to stand behind the yes. It is not the other person's ability, and it would not have fixed a missing net.

items.example:
Swimming pool, Saturday, 8:00am.
Coach: “Yes, you can go to the deep end. Hold the rail, and I'll stand by the steps.”
Girl: “Okay.”

items.text: It is Thursday, 5:00pm. You fly out at nine tonight and are away for two weeks. Clara asks to take the biggest client call alone on Friday.
options: Give the yes now. A yes that is put off is a yes refused.
Hold the big yes until you can be reachable, or give it for something smaller. Steiner says a major permission should be given only when you can also be there for the fear that follows.
Say no flatly. If she wants it, she should have planned better.
items.why: Steiner says the timing of a permission matters. A major yes should not be given just before you go away or when your schedule is full, because the protection that has to follow would not be there.

traps.0: Give the yes now. It feels generous, and putting it off feels like a refusal. But a big yes with nobody to catch her is the bare green light again.
traps.2: Say no flatly. It protects you from the risk, but it shuts the door on her and teaches her to stop asking. Holding the yes for later is different from refusing it.

items.example:
Hill walk, Friday, 3:00pm.
Guide: “You can lead the group tomorrow. But I'm off the radio until Monday, so the route you lead is the short one.”
Walker: “That works.”

debrief.nadia: A yes on its own is a door left open with nobody in the room. Give the reason she can believe, be there for the fear that comes after, and keep the yes standing when someone leans on it. Give the green light only when you can do all three.
debrief.bookNote: The books call these permission, protection and potency. Steiner's permission frees a person from an old order, protection means the giver is there for the fear that follows, and potency is the giver's strength to match the old order; protection was first set out by Patricia Crossman.

reflection.prompt: Think of one yes you gave this week. Did you give a reason, stay reachable afterwards, and hold the yes when someone pushed against it?
